pages.text: "Soso, the postman is coming!" Grandma Bear, who ran the lodge, opened the door wide. Soso the quiet hedgehog hid behind a log by the door. Mr. Badger climbed the slope with a backpack.
A white letter stuck out above the backpack. From behind the log, Soso whispered, "I hope that's my letter..." A cousin below the mountain had promised to write.
Mr. Badger took out the letter. "Who is Soso?" Soso tried to answer, but their spines bristled, and their body curled into a ball. No sound came out.
The letter went back above the backpack. "Then I'll come another time." Mr. Badger went down the slope. Soso only watched from behind the log.
The white letter disappeared between the trees. Soso's nose turned red. Grandma sat beside Soso. "Your words were pressed down beneath your spines."
Grandma slowly stroked Soso's back with her palm. The spines settled. "When your spines lie down, your voice can come out." Grandma said like a song, "Spines down, say hello!"
Soso practiced in front of the log. A breath out, and spines down. "Hello." Soft, but a sound! Grandma brought her hands together and smiled gently.
The next day, the backpack came up the slope again. Soso curled into a ball, then slowly straightened. "Hello! I'm Soso!" The voice rang all the way to the door.
Mr. Badger placed the white letter in Soso's hand. "One, spines down! Two, look them in the eyes! Three, hello!" Soso hugged the letter to their chest.

Grandma wrapped an arm around Soso's back, and they read together. One greeting brings what you've waited for into your hands. In Grandma's arms, Soso said, "Now I can greet people too. Spines down, say hello!"
